1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * BK7258 PWC worker and CPU1 ready handshake.
3:  ****************************************************************************/
4: 
5: #include <nuttx/config.h>
6: #include <stdint.h>
7: #include <stdbool.h>
8: #include <stdio.h>
9: 
10: #include <nuttx/semaphore.h>
11: #include <nuttx/sched.h>
12: #include <nuttx/signal.h>
13: #include <nuttx/kthread.h>
14: #include <nuttx/clock.h>
15: 
16: #include "bk7258_psram.h"
17: #include "hardware/bk7258_mbox.h"
18: 
19: #define PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD 0x5u
20: #define PM_CTRL_PSRAM_POWER_CMD 0x7u
21: #define PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD 0x8u
22: #define PM_CP1_DUMP_PSRAM_MALLOC_INFO_CMD 0x9u
23: #define PM_CP1_RECOVERY_CMD 0xau
24: #define PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_CPU1 11u
25: #define PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON 0u
26: #define PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF 1u
27: #define PM_RECOVERY_STATE_INIT 0u
28: #define PM_RECOVERY_STATE_FINISH 1u
29: #define PM_QUEUE_DEPTH 8u
30: #define PM_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS 500u
31: #define PM_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS 1000u
32: 
33: struct pwc_message
34: {
35:   uint32_t header;
36:   uint32_t param1;
37:   uint32_t param2;
38:   uint32_t param3;
39: };
40: 
41: static struct pwc_message g_queue[PM_QUEUE_DEPTH];
42: static volatile unsigned int g_head;
43: static volatile unsigned int g_tail;
44: static sem_t g_pwc_sem;
45: static sem_t g_worker_sem;
46: static sem_t g_psram_power_sem;
47: static volatile bool g_worker_ready;
48: static volatile bool g_ready_sent;
49: static volatile bool g_psram_power_waiting;
50: static volatile uint32_t g_psram_power_state;
51: 
52: static void psram_power_vote_rollback(void)
53: {
54:   int ret;
55: 
56:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(PM_CTRL_PSRAM_POWER_CMD,
57:                                 PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_CPU1,
58:                                 PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF, 0);
59:   if (ret >= 0)
60:     {
61:       ret = bk7258_mailbox_wait_pwc(PM_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS);
62:     }
63: 
64:   if (ret < 0)
65:     {
66:       printf("PWC: PSRAM power vote rollback failed, error=%d\n", ret);
67:     }
68: }
69: 
70: static int ipc_heartbeat_worker(int argc, char **argv)
71: {
72:   static uint32_t heartbeat_payload;
73: 
74:   (void)argc;
75:   (void)argv;
76:   for (;;)
77:     {
78:       nxsig_usleep(2000000);
79:       (void)bk7258_mbox_send_message(2, 0x10,
80:                                      (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)&heartbeat_payload,
81:                                      sizeof(heartbeat_payload), 0);
82:     }
83:   return 0;
84: }
85: 
86: static void pwc_rx(const void *raw)
87: {
88:   const uint8_t *bytes = raw;
89:   struct pwc_message message;
90:   unsigned int next = (g_head + 1u) % PM_QUEUE_DEPTH;
91:   if (next == g_tail || bytes == NULL)
92:     {
93:       return;
94:     }
95:   message.header = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[0];
96:   message.param1 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[1];
97:   message.param2 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[2];
98:   message.param3 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[3];
99:   g_queue[g_head] = message;
100:   g_head = next;
101:   nxsem_post(&g_pwc_sem);
102: }
103: 
104: static int pwc_worker(int argc, char **argv)
105: {
106:   (void)argc;
107:   (void)argv;
108:   g_worker_ready = true;
109:   nxsem_post(&g_worker_sem);
110:   for (;;)
111:     {
112:       struct pwc_message message;
113:       nxsem_wait_uninterruptible(&g_pwc_sem);
114:       message = g_queue[g_tail];
115:       g_tail = (g_tail + 1u) % PM_QUEUE_DEPTH;
116:       /* Hardware power/clock actions stay in this thread, never in IRQ. */
117:       switch (message.header & 0xffu)
118:         {
119:           case PM_CTRL_PSRAM_POWER_CMD:
120:             /* The unmodified AVDK SMP firmware returns the requested ON/OFF
121:              * state in param1. It does not expose the PSRAM driver result or
122:              * detected capacity, so AP validates its configured regions with
123:              * the non-destructive boundary probe before creating allocators.
124:              */
125: 
126:             g_psram_power_state = message.param1;
127:             if (g_psram_power_waiting)
128:               {
129:                 g_psram_power_waiting = false;
130:                 nxsem_post(&g_psram_power_sem);
131:               }
132:             break;
133: 
134: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_PSRAM
135:           case PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD:
136:             if (message.param1 == 0u)
137:               {
138:                 (void)bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(
139:                   PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD,
140:                   PM_CP1_PSRAM_MALLOC_STATE_CMD,
141:                   bk7258_psram_heap_used(), 0);
142:               }
143:             else if (message.param1 == PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF)
144:               {
145:                 /* This CP notification is sent after physical power-down. */
146: 
147:                 bk7258_psram_power_lost();
148:               }
149:             break;
150: 
151:           case PM_CP1_DUMP_PSRAM_MALLOC_INFO_CMD:
152:             bk7258_psram_dump();
153:             break;
154: 
155:           case PM_CP1_RECOVERY_CMD:
156:             {
157:               int ret = bk7258_psram_shutdown();
158: 
159:               (void)bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(
160:                 PM_CP1_RECOVERY_CMD, PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_CPU1,
161:                 ret == 0 ? PM_RECOVERY_STATE_FINISH :
162:                            PM_RECOVERY_STATE_INIT, 0);
163:             }
164:             break;
165: #endif
166: 
167:           default:
168:             break;
169:         }
170:     }
171:   return 0;
172: }
173: 
174: int bk7258_pwc_start(void)
175: {
176:   int pid;
177:   int ret;
178: 
179:   nxsem_init(&g_pwc_sem, 0, 0);
180:   nxsem_init(&g_worker_sem, 0, 0);
181:   nxsem_init(&g_psram_power_sem, 0, 0);
182:   g_head = 0;
183:   g_tail = 0;
184:   g_worker_ready = false;
185:   g_ready_sent = false;
186:   g_psram_power_waiting = false;
187:   g_psram_power_state = PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_OFF;
188:   bk7258_mailbox_set_pwc_rx(pwc_rx);
189:   /* Match Armino mb_ipc_heartbeat: notify CPU0 before PM ready and keep the
190:    * CPU1 liveness indication independent from the PWC worker. */
191:   if (bk7258_mbox_send_message(1, 0x10, 0, 0, 0) != 0)
192:     {
193:       return -1;
194:     }
195: 
196:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_wait_hw_control(PM_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS);
197:   if (ret < 0)
198:     {
199:       printf("PWC: IPC power-up transport timeout, error=%d\n", ret);
200:       bk7258_mailbox_dump_stats();
201:       return ret;
202:     }
203:   printf("PWC: IPC power-up transport complete\n");
204: 
205:   if (kthread_create("ipc-heartbeat", 100, 1536, ipc_heartbeat_worker,
206:                      NULL) < 0)
207:     {
208:       return -1;
209:     }
210:   pid = kthread_create("pwc", 110, 2048, pwc_worker, NULL);
211:   if (pid < 0)
212:     {
213:       return pid;
214:     }
215:   if (nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible(&g_worker_sem, MSEC2TICK(200)) < 0 ||
216:       !g_worker_ready)
217:     {
218:       printf("PWC: worker start timeout\n");
219:       bk7258_mailbox_dump_stats();
220:       return -ETIMEDOUT;
221:     }
222:   printf("PWC: worker ready\n");
223: 
224:   /* CP boots CPU1 from its low-power worker and waits there for this ready
225:    * command. Send it before requesting PSRAM, whose vote is handled by that
226:    * same worker, otherwise the two cores deadlock waiting for each other.
227:    */
228: 
229:   g_ready_sent = bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(PM_CPU1_BOOT_READY_CMD,
230:                                          1, 0, 0) == 0;
231:   if (!g_ready_sent)
232:     {
233:       printf("PWC: CPU1 boot-ready queue failed\n");
234:       bk7258_mailbox_dump_stats();
235:       return -EIO;
236:     }
237: 
238:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_wait_pwc(PM_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS);
239:   if (ret < 0)
240:     {
241:       printf("PWC: CPU1 boot-ready transport timeout, error=%d\n", ret);
242:       bk7258_mailbox_dump_stats();
243:       return ret;
244:     }
245: 
246:   printf("PWC: CPU1 boot-ready acknowledged by CP transport\n");
247: 
248: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_PSRAM
249:   g_psram_power_waiting = true;
250:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_pwc(PM_CTRL_PSRAM_POWER_CMD,
251:                                 PM_POWER_PSRAM_MODULE_CPU1,
252:                                 PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON, 0);
253:   if (ret >= 0)
254:     {
255:       ret = nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible(&g_psram_power_sem,
256:                          MSEC2TICK(PM_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS));
257:     }
258: 
259:   g_psram_power_waiting = false;
260:   if (ret < 0 || g_psram_power_state != PM_POWER_MODULE_STATE_ON)
261:     {
262:       printf("PWC: PSRAM power response failed, error=%d state=%lu\n",
263:              ret, (unsigned long)g_psram_power_state);
264:       bk7258_mailbox_dump_stats();
265:       psram_power_vote_rollback();
266: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_PSRAM_REQUIRED
267:       return ret < 0 ? ret : -EIO;
268: #endif
269:     }
270:   else
271:     {
272:       /* printf("PWC: PSRAM power vote ON acknowledged\n"); */
273:       ret = bk7258_psram_initialize();
274:       if (ret < 0)
275:         {
276:           printf("PWC: PSRAM allocator initialization failed, error=%d\n",
277:                  ret);
278:           psram_power_vote_rollback();
279: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_PSRAM_REQUIRED
280:           return ret;
281: #endif
282:         }
283:       else
284:         {
285:           /* printf("PWC: PSRAM allocators ONLINE\n"); */
286:         }
287:     }
288: #endif
289: 
290:   if (g_ready_sent)
291:     {
292:       return 0;
293:     }
294: 
295:   return -1;
296: }

143: static bool valid_ack(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *ack)

150: static void mb_uart_tx_complete(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *ack,
151:                                 int result, void *arg)
152: {
153:   irqstate_t flags;
154:   uint8_t command;
155:   bool failed;
156: 
157:   (void)arg;
158:   flags = up_irq_save();
159:   command = ack == NULL ? g_uart.transaction_command :
160:             bk7258_mb_header_cmd(ack);
161:   failed = result < 0 || !valid_ack(ack) ||
162:            (ack != NULL && (ack->payload_address & 2u) != 0);
163: 
164:   if (ack != NULL && valid_ack(ack))
165:     {
166:       g_uart.peer_rts = (ack->payload_address & 1u) != 0;
167:       g_uart.peer_rts_known = true;
168:     }
169: 
170:   if (result == -ETIMEDOUT || result == -ECONNRESET)
171:     {
172:       g_uart.peer_rts_known = false;
173:       g_uart.state_pending = true;
174:     }
175: 
176:   if (command == BK7258_MB_UART_DATA && g_uart.tx_inflight != 0)
177:     {
178:       if (!failed)
179:         {
180:           g_uart.tx_read = (g_uart.tx_read + g_uart.tx_inflight) %
181:                            MB_UART_TX_SIZE;
182:           g_uart.tx_retry_count = 0;
183:         }
184:       else if (result == -ETIMEDOUT || result == -ECONNRESET)
185:         {
186:           /* A failed/unknown ACK cannot tell whether CP consumed the bytes.
187:            * Drop this local chunk rather than replaying terminal characters.
188:            */
189: 
190:           g_uart.tx_read = (g_uart.tx_read + g_uart.tx_inflight) %
191:                            MB_UART_TX_SIZE;
192:           g_uart.stats.tx_unknown++;
193:           g_uart.tx_retry_count = 0;
194:           g_uart.stats.resets++;
195:         }
196:       else
197:         {
198:           g_uart.stats.remote_fail++;
199:           g_uart.state_pending = true;
200:           if (g_uart.tx_retry_count == 0)
201:             {
202:               /* Keep tx_read unchanged.  The same chunk may be copied again
203:                * once STATE recovery succeeds, but only once.
204:                */
205: 
206:               g_uart.tx_retry_count = 1;
207:               g_uart.stats.tx_retry++;
208:             }
209:           else
210:             {
211:               g_uart.tx_read = (g_uart.tx_read + g_uart.tx_inflight) %
212:                                MB_UART_TX_SIZE;
213:               g_uart.tx_retry_count = 0;
214:               g_uart.stats.tx_retry_drop++;
215:             }
216:         }
217: 
218:       g_uart.tx_inflight = 0;
219:     }
220:   else if (command == BK7258_MB_UART_STATE && failed)
221:     {
222:       g_uart.stats.remote_fail++;
223:       /* The transport invokes this completion before it changes READY to
224:        * ABORTING.  Always retain a STATE request so RESET recovery has a
225:        * probe to send after it reaches PROBING.
226:        */
227: 
228:       g_uart.state_pending = true;
229:     }
230: 
231:   g_uart.transaction_busy = false;
232:   up_irq_restore(flags);
233:   nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
234: }

236: static int mb_uart_receive(const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message,
237:                            uint8_t *ack_flags, void *arg)
238: {

241:   uint16_t first;
242:   bool failed = false;
243:   bool malformed = false;
244: 
245:   (void)arg;
246:   if (ack_flags == NULL)
247:     {
248:       return -EINVAL;
249:     }
250: 
251:   if (command != BK7258_MB_UART_DATA && command != BK7258_MB_UART_STATE)
252:     {
253:       g_uart.stats.bad_flags++;
254:       failed = true;
255:       malformed = true;
256:     }
257:   else if ((message->flags & ~1u) != 0)

259:       g_uart.stats.bad_flags++;
260:       failed = true;
261:       malformed = true;
262:     }
263:   else if (message->crc8 != 0)
264:     {
265:       g_uart.stats.bad_crc++;
266:       g_uart.sticky_status |= MB_UART_STATUS_PARITY;
267:       failed = true;
268:       malformed = true;
269:     }
270:   else if (message->reserved != 0)
271:     {
272:       g_uart.stats.bad_reserved++;
273:       failed = true;
274:       malformed = true;
275:     }
276: 
277:   if (!failed && command == BK7258_MB_UART_DATA)
278:     {
279:       if (message->payload_address != BK7258_MB_UART_RX_ADDRESS)
280:         {
281:           g_uart.stats.bad_pointer++;
282:           failed = true;
283:           malformed = true;
284:         }
285:       else if (length == 0 || length > BK7258_MB_UART_CHUNK_SIZE)
286:         {
287:           g_uart.stats.bad_length++;
288:           failed = true;
289:           malformed = true;
290:         }
291:       else if (!bk7258_mailbox_link_ready())
292:         {
293:           failed = true;
294:         }
295:       else if (rx_free() < length)
296:         {
297:           g_uart.stats.rx_overflow++;
298:           g_uart.sticky_status |= MB_UART_STATUS_OVF;
299:           failed = true;
300:         }
301:       else
302:         {
303:           const uint8_t *source =
304:             (const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)BK7258_MB_UART_RX_ADDRESS;
305: 
306:           __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
307:           first = MB_UART_RX_SIZE - g_uart.rx_write;
308:           if (first > length)
309:             {
310:               first = length;
311:             }
312: 
313:           memcpy(&g_uart.rx_ring[g_uart.rx_write], source, first);
314:           if (first != length)
315:             {
316:               memcpy(g_uart.rx_ring, source + first, length - first);
317:             }
318: 
319:           g_uart.rx_write = (g_uart.rx_write + length) % MB_UART_RX_SIZE;
320:           g_uart.stats.data_rx++;
321:           g_uart.stats.rx_bytes += length;
322:         }
323:     }
324:   else if (!failed)
325:     {
326:       if (message->payload_address != 0 || message->payload_length != 0)
327:         {
328:           g_uart.stats.bad_length++;
329:           failed = true;
330:           malformed = true;
331:         }
332:       else
333:         {
334:           g_uart.stats.state_rx++;
335:         }
336:     }
337: 
338:   if (!malformed)
339:     {
340:       bool old_peer_rts = g_uart.peer_rts;
341: 
342:       g_uart.peer_rts = (message->flags & 1u) != 0;
343:       g_uart.peer_rts_known = true;
344:       if (old_peer_rts && !g_uart.peer_rts)
345:         {
346:           nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
347:         }
348:     }
349: 
350:   update_local_rts();
351:   *ack_flags = (g_uart.local_rts ? 1u : 0u) | (failed ? 2u : 0u);
352:   nxsem_post(&g_uart.worker_sem);
353:   return malformed ? -EPROTO : OK;
354: }

356: static int send_state_locked(void)
357: {
358:   struct bk7258_mb_wire_message message;
359:   int ret;
360: 
361:   memset(&message, 0, sizeof(message));
362:   message.header = bk7258_mb_make_header(BK7258_MB_UART_STATE, 0, 0, 0,
363:                                          BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX);
364:   message.flags = g_uart.local_rts ? 1u : 0u;

366:                                   mb_uart_tx_complete, NULL);

370:       g_uart.transaction_command = BK7258_MB_UART_STATE;
371:       g_uart.state_pending = false;

384:   uint16_t first;
385:   int ret;

389:       length = BK7258_MB_UART_CHUNK_SIZE;

403:   memcpy(destination, &g_uart.tx_ring[g_uart.tx_read], first);

406:       memcpy(destination + first, g_uart.tx_ring, length - first);
407:     }
408: 
409:   memset(&message, 0, sizeof(message));
410:   message.header = bk7258_mb_make_header(BK7258_MB_UART_DATA, 0, 0, 0,
411:                                          BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX);
412:   message.payload_address = BK7258_MB_UART_TX_ADDRESS;
413:   message.payload_length = length;
414:   message.flags = g_uart.local_rts ? 1u : 0u;
415:   __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
416:   ret = bk7258_mailbox_send_wire(BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX, &message,
417:                                   mb_uart_tx_complete, NULL);

429: static int mb_uart_worker(int argc, char **argv)
430: {
431:   (void)argc;
432:   (void)argv;
433: 
434:   for (;;)
435:     {
436:       bk7258_mb_uart_callback_t callback;

22: 
23:   (void)channel;
24:   return bk7258_mbox_uart_write(&byte, 1) == 1 ? ch : EOF;

31:   if (ret != EOF && !up_interrupt_context())

33:       (void)bk7258_mbox_uart_flush(BK7258_SYSLOG_FORCE_TIMEOUT_MS);
34:     }
35: 
36:   return ret;

39: static ssize_t bk7258_syslog_write(syslog_channel_t *channel,
40:                                    const char *buffer, size_t length)
41: {
42:   size_t total = 0;
43: 
44:   (void)channel;
45:   while (total < length)
46:     {
47:       size_t chunk = length - total;
48:       ssize_t ret;
49: 
50:       if (chunk > UINT16_MAX)
51:         {
52:           chunk = UINT16_MAX;
53:         }
54: 
55:       ret = bk7258_mbox_uart_write((const uint8_t *)buffer + total, chunk);
56:       if (ret <= 0)
57:         {
58:           return total != 0 ? (ssize_t)total : ret;
59:         }
60: 
61:       total += ret;
62:       if ((size_t)ret < chunk)
63:         {
64:           break;
65:         }
66:     }
67: 
68:   return total;
69: }

75:

79:     }

58: void bk7258_gpio_set_function(unsigned int pin, unsigned int function);
59: 
60: static int bk7258_pwm_setup(struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *dev);
61: static int bk7258_pwm_shutdown(struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *dev);
62: static int bk7258_pwm_start(struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *dev,
63:                             const struct pwm_info_s *info);
64: static int bk7258_pwm_stop(struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *dev);
65: static int bk7258_pwm_ioctl(struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *dev, int cmd,
66:                             unsigned long arg);
67: 
68: static const struct pwm_ops_s g_pwm_ops =
69: {
70:   .setup = bk7258_pwm_setup,
71:   .shutdown = bk7258_pwm_shutdown,
72:   .start = bk7258_pwm_start,
73:   .stop = bk7258_pwm_stop,
74:   .ioctl = bk7258_pwm_ioctl,
75: };
76: 
77: static struct bk7258_pwm_lowerhalf_s g_motor_pwm =
78: {
79:   .ops = &g_pwm_ops,
80: };
81: 
82: static int bk7258_pwm_setup(struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *dev)
83: {
84:   struct bk7258_pwm_lowerhalf_s *priv =
85:     (struct bk7258_pwm_lowerhalf_s *)dev;
86:   irqstate_t flags;
87: 
88:   flags = enter_critical_section();
89:   modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_CLKSEL, 0, BK7258_SYS_PWM0_CLKSEL);
90:   modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_CLK_ENABLE, 0, BK7258_SYS_PWM0_CLK_ENABLE);
91:   putreg32(1, BK7258_PWM_CG_RESET);
92:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(BK7258_MOTOR_PWM_GPIO, BK7258_GPIO_FUNC_PWM3);
93:   bk7258_gpio_output(BK7258_MOTOR_LDO_GPIO, false);
94:   priv->setup = true;
95:   leave_critical_section(flags);
96: 
97:   return OK;
98: }
99: 
100: static int bk7258_pwm_shutdown(struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *dev)
101: {
102:   struct bk7258_pwm_lowerhalf_s *priv =
103:     (struct bk7258_pwm_lowerhalf_s *)dev;
104: 
105:   bk7258_pwm_stop(dev);
106:   modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_CLK_ENABLE, BK7258_SYS_PWM0_CLK_ENABLE, 0);
107:   priv->setup = false;
108:   return OK;
109: }
110: 
111: static int bk7258_pwm_start(struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *dev,
112:                             const struct pwm_info_s *info)
113: {
114:   struct bk7258_pwm_lowerhalf_s *priv =
115:     (struct bk7258_pwm_lowerhalf_s *)dev;
116:   uint64_t period;
117:   uint64_t duty;
118:   irqstate_t flags;
119: 
120:   if (!priv->setup || info == NULL || info->frequency == 0)
121:     {
122:       return -EINVAL;
123:     }
124: 
125:   period = BK7258_PWM_CLOCK_HZ / info->frequency;
126:   if (period < 2 || period > UINT32_MAX)
127:     {
128:       return -ERANGE;
129:     }
130: 
131:   duty = (period * info->duty) >> 16;
132:   if (duty > period)
133:     {
134:       duty = period;
135:     }
136: 
137:   flags = enter_critical_section();
138:   modifyreg32(BK7258_PWM_CR1, BK7258_PWM_CR1_CEN2, 0);
139:   modifyreg32(BK7258_PWM_CR1, 0,
140:               BK7258_PWM_CR1_ARPE2 | BK7258_PWM_CR1_OC2PE);
141:   modifyreg32(BK7258_PWM_PRESCALER, BK7258_PWM_PSC2_MASK, 0);
142:   putreg32((uint32_t)period - 1u, BK7258_PWM_TIM2_ARR);
143:   putreg32((uint32_t)(period - duty), BK7258_PWM_CCR4);
144:   putreg32((uint32_t)period, BK7258_PWM_CCR5);
145:   modifyreg32(BK7258_PWM_CCMR,
146:               BK7258_PWM_CCMR_TIM2CCM | BK7258_PWM_CCMR_OC2M_MASK,
147:               BK7258_PWM_CCMR_CH4E |
148:               (duty == 0 ? BK7258_PWM_CCMR_OC2M_LOW :
149:                duty == period ? BK7258_PWM_CCMR_OC2M_HIGH :
150:                BK7258_PWM_CCMR_OC2M_TOGGLE));
151:   modifyreg32(BK7258_PWM_EDTR, 0, BK7258_PWM_EDTR_UG2);
152:   modifyreg32(BK7258_PWM_CR1, 0, BK7258_PWM_CR1_CEN2);
153:   bk7258_gpio_write(BK7258_MOTOR_LDO_GPIO, duty != 0);
154:   leave_critical_section(flags);
155: 
156:   return OK;
157: }
158: 
159: static int bk7258_pwm_stop(struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *dev)
160: {
161:   irqstate_t flags;
162: 
163:   (void)dev;
164:   flags = enter_critical_section();
165:   modifyreg32(BK7258_PWM_CCMR, BK7258_PWM_CCMR_CH4E, 0);
166:   modifyreg32(BK7258_PWM_CR1, BK7258_PWM_CR1_CEN2, 0);
167:   bk7258_gpio_write(BK7258_MOTOR_LDO_GPIO, false);
168:   leave_critical_section(flags);
169: 
170:   return OK;
171: }

173: static int bk7258_pwm_ioctl(struct pwm_lowerhalf_s *dev, int cmd,
174:                             unsigned long arg)
175: {
176:   (void)dev;
177:   (void)cmd;
178:   (void)arg;
179:   return -ENOTTY;
180: }

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_dma.c
3:  *
4:  * BK7258 minimal single-channel (channel 0), single-shot, memory-to-memory
5:  * DMA driver.  Register layout source: bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
6:  * ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/dma_struct.h and hal/dma_ll.h.
7:  *
8:  * Register offsets (byte offset from BK7258_DMA_BASE, word index in
9:  * dma_hw_t from dma_struct.h in parentheses):
10:  *   config_group[0] starts at byte offset 0x40 (word index 0x10): the
11:  *   dma_hw_t header occupies 16 words (device_id, version_id, prio_mode,
12:  *   reg_gap_0, secure_attr, privileged_attr, int_status0~3, int_allocate,
13:  *   reg_gap_1[5] = 0x0..0xF).  Each channel occupies 16 words (0x40 bytes):
14:  *     ctrl              word 0  (REG_0x10) - bit[0] enable, bit[1]
15:  *                                finish_int_en, bit[3] mode(0=SINGLE),
16:  *                                bit[8] src_addr_inc_en, bit[9]
17:  *                                dest_addr_inc_en, bit[16:31] transfer_len
18:  *     dest_start_addr    word 1  (REG_0x11)
19:  *     src_start_addr     word 2  (REG_0x12)
20:  *     req_mux            word 7  (REG_0x17) - not used by this driver
21:  *                                (memory-to-memory transfer, matching
22:  *                                bk_dvp.c's encode_yuv_dma_cpy() which uses
23:  *                                DMA_DEV_DTCM on both ends and never touches
24:  *                                req_mux)
25:  *     status             word 12 (REG_0x1c) - bit[0:16] remain_len,
26:  *                                bit[18] finish_int
27:  *
28:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
29:  ****************************************************************************/
30: 
31: #include <nuttx/config.h>
32: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
33: #include <nuttx/irq.h>
34: #include <stdbool.h>
35: #include <stdint.h>
36: 
37: #include "arm_internal.h"
38: #include "irq.h"
39: #include "bk7258_dma.h"
40: 
41: #define BK7258_DMA_BASE            0x45020000u  /* SOC_GENER_DMA_REG_BASE */
42: #define BK7258_DMA_CHANNEL         0u
43: 
44: #define BK7258_DMA_CHAN_GROUP_BASE (BK7258_DMA_BASE + 0x40u)
45: #define BK7258_DMA_CHAN_STRIDE     0x40u  /* 16 words * 4 bytes per channel */
46: 
47: #define BK7258_DMA_REG(word_off)  (BK7258_DMA_CHAN_GROUP_BASE + \
48:                                     BK7258_DMA_CHANNEL * BK7258_DMA_CHAN_STRIDE + \
49:                                     (word_off) * 4u)
50: 
51: #define BK7258_DMA_CTRL            BK7258_DMA_REG(0)
52: #define BK7258_DMA_DEST_ADDR       BK7258_DMA_REG(1)
53: #define BK7258_DMA_SRC_ADDR        BK7258_DMA_REG(2)
54: #define BK7258_DMA_STATUS          BK7258_DMA_REG(12)
55: 
56: #define BK7258_DMA_CTRL_ENABLE          (1u << 0)
57: #define BK7258_DMA_CTRL_FINISH_INT_EN   (1u << 1)
58: #define BK7258_DMA_CTRL_MODE_SINGLE     (0u << 3)
59: #define BK7258_DMA_CTRL_SRC_INC_EN      (1u << 8)
60: #define BK7258_DMA_CTRL_DEST_INC_EN     (1u << 9)
61: #define BK7258_DMA_CTRL_LEN_SHIFT       16u
62: #define BK7258_DMA_CTRL_LEN_MASK        0xffffu
63: 
64: #define BK7258_DMA_STATUS_REMAIN_LEN_MASK 0x1ffffu
65: #define BK7258_DMA_STATUS_FINISH_INT      (1u << 18)
66: 
67: static bk7258_dma_done_cb_t g_done_cb;
68: static void *g_done_cb_arg;
69: 
70: static int bk7258_dma_isr(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
71: {
72:   uint32_t status = getreg32(BK7258_DMA_STATUS);
73: 
74:   if ((status & BK7258_DMA_STATUS_FINISH_INT) != 0)
75:     {
76:       /* Stop the channel (clears enable so a stale "finish" state from
77:        * this transfer does not confuse the next bk7258_dma_configure()
78:        * call) and acknowledge the finish flag by writing it back (the
79:        * status register's finish_int bit is part of the same word as
80:        * remain_len; per dma_struct.h there is no separate write-1-to-clear
81:        * register documented for this field in the excerpt reviewed, so we
82:        * rely on disabling the channel via ctrl.enable=0, which is what
83:        * bk_dvp.c's line-done handlers do via bk_dma_stop() before
84:        * reconfiguring for the next transfer). */
85:       modifyreg32(BK7258_DMA_CTRL, BK7258_DMA_CTRL_ENABLE, 0);
86: 
87:       if (g_done_cb != NULL)
88:         {
89:           g_done_cb(g_done_cb_arg);
90:         }
91:     }
92: 
93:   return 0;
94: }
95: 
96: void bk7258_dma_init(void)
97: {
98:   modifyreg32(BK7258_DMA_CTRL, BK7258_DMA_CTRL_ENABLE, 0);
99: 
100:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_DMA, bk7258_dma_isr, NULL);
101:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_DMA);
102: }
103: 
104: void bk7258_dma_configure(uint32_t src_addr, uint32_t dest_addr,
105:                            uint32_t transfer_len)
106: {
107:   uint32_t ctrl;
108:   uint32_t len_field;
109: 
110:   /* Ensure the channel is disabled before reprogramming, matching
111:    * bk_dvp.c's yuv_sm0_line_done()/yuv_sm1_line_done() pattern of calling
112:    * bk_dma_stop() before bk_dma_set_src_start_addr()/
113:    * bk_dma_set_dest_start_addr()/bk_dma_start() on each line-done
114:    * interrupt. */
115:   modifyreg32(BK7258_DMA_CTRL, BK7258_DMA_CTRL_ENABLE, 0);
116: 
117:   putreg32(src_addr, BK7258_DMA_SRC_ADDR);
118:   putreg32(dest_addr, BK7258_DMA_DEST_ADDR);
119: 
120:   /* transfer_len is in bytes (matching bk_dma_set_transfer_len()'s
121:    * "over 65536 bytes" bounds-check message).  The ctrl.transfer_len
122:    * register field encodes (byte_count - 1), per
123:    * dma_ll_set_transfer_len(): "ctrl.transfer_len = (tran_len - 1) &
124:    * 0xffff" (ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/dma_ll.h:371). */
125:   len_field = (transfer_len - 1u) & BK7258_DMA_CTRL_LEN_MASK;
126: 
127:   ctrl = BK7258_DMA_CTRL_MODE_SINGLE |
128:          BK7258_DMA_CTRL_SRC_INC_EN |
129:          BK7258_DMA_CTRL_DEST_INC_EN |
130:          BK7258_DMA_CTRL_FINISH_INT_EN |
131:          (len_field << BK7258_DMA_CTRL_LEN_SHIFT);
132: 
133:   putreg32(ctrl, BK7258_DMA_CTRL);
134: }
135: 
136: void bk7258_dma_set_done_callback(bk7258_dma_done_cb_t cb, void *arg)
137: {
138:   g_done_cb = cb;
139:   g_done_cb_arg = arg;
140: }
141: 
142: void bk7258_dma_start(void)
143: {
144:   modifyreg32(BK7258_DMA_CTRL, 0, BK7258_DMA_CTRL_ENABLE);
145: }
146: 
147: void bk7258_dma_stop(void)
148: {
149:   modifyreg32(BK7258_DMA_CTRL, BK7258_DMA_CTRL_ENABLE, 0);
150: }
151: 
152: bool bk7258_dma_is_busy(void)
153: {
154:   return (getreg32(BK7258_DMA_CTRL) & BK7258_DMA_CTRL_ENABLE) != 0;
155: }
156: 
157: uint32_t bk7258_dma_get_remain_len(void)
158: {
159:   return getreg32(BK7258_DMA_STATUS) & BK7258_DMA_STATUS_REMAIN_LEN_MASK;
160: }

(End of file - total 160 lines)

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_i2c1.c
3:  *
4:  * Interrupt-driven hardware I2C1 master-write driver.  See
5:  * include/bk7258_i2c1.h for the full rationale (why this board needs
6:  * hardware I2C1 on GPIO42/43 instead of the previous bk7258_i2c_sim.c
7:  * bit-banged GPIO0/1 driver).
8:  *
9:  * State machine and register-access sequencing are a from-scratch
10:  * reimplementation of bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
11:  * ap/middleware/driver/i2c/i2c_driver.c's I2C_MASTER_WRITE path
12:  * (i2c_hardware_memory_write_impl() -> i2c_master_start() ->
13:  * i2c_master_set_write_dev_addr() -> i2c_master_write_mem_addr_low_8bit()
14:  * -> i2c1_master_write_data() -> i2c_master_stop()), driven by
15:  * i2c1_isr_common()'s per-byte-ACK interrupt handling.  Register bit
16:  * layout: hardware/bk7258_i2c1.h (ported from that release's
17:  * i2c_struct.h/i2c_reg.h).
18:  *
19:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
20:  ****************************************************************************/
21: 
22: #include <nuttx/config.h>
23: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
24: #include <nuttx/irq.h>
25: #include <nuttx/semaphore.h>
26: #include <nuttx/spinlock.h>
27: #include <stdbool.h>
28: #include <stdint.h>
29: #include <stdio.h>
30: 
31: #include "arm_internal.h"
32: #include "irq.h"
33: #include "bk7258_gpio.h"
34: #include "bk7258_i2c1.h"
35: #include "hardware/bk7258_i2c1.h"
36: #include "hardware/bk7258_sysctrl.h"
37: 
38: /* GPIO42/GPIO43 pinmux function index for I2C1_SCL/I2C1_SDA.
39:  *
40:  * bk_avdk_smp ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_map.h's per-pin
41:  * function array for GPIO_42 is:
42:  *   {GPIO_DEV_I2C1_SCL, GPIO_DEV_I2S2_DIN, GPIO_DEV_LIN_SLEEP,
43:  *    GPIO_DEV_SCR_RSTN, GPIO_DEV_LCD_G2, GPIO_DEV_DEBUG30,
44:  *    GPIO_DEV_INVALID, GPIO_DEV_SLCD_SEG1}
45:  * i.e. GPIO_DEV_I2C1_SCL is array index 0.  GPIO_43's array is the same
46:  * shape with GPIO_DEV_I2C1_SDA at index 0.  bk7258_gpio_set_function()'s
47:  * "function" parameter is this array index (see bk7258_gpio.c: it writes
48:  * `function & 0xf` into the 4-bit-per-pin GPIO_SYS_CFG pinmux-select
49:  * field). */
50: #define BK7258_I2C1_SCL_PIN       42u
51: #define BK7258_I2C1_SDA_PIN       43u
52: #define BK7258_I2C1_PINMUX_FUNCTION 0u
53: 
54: /* 100kHz standard-mode I2C, matching GC2145's supported bus speed and
55:  * gsensor_sc7a20.c's i2c_cfg.baud_rate=100000 convention for this SoC
56:  * family. */
57: #define BK7258_I2C1_BAUD_RATE     100000u
58: 
59: /* freq_div formula: bk_avdk_smp ap/middleware/soc/common/hal/i2c_hal.c
60:  * I2C_CLK_DIVID(rate) = ROUND_UP(ROUND_UP(CONFIG_XTAL_FREQ, rate) - 6, 3)
61:  * - 1.  CONFIG_XTAL_FREQ for this board's 26MHz crystal (schematic sheet
62:  * 2/6, "26M,12pF,85C" crystal note) is 26000000. */
63: #define BK7258_I2C1_XTAL_FREQ     26000000u
64: #define BK7258_I2C1_ROUND_UP(a, b) (((a) / (b)) + (((a) % (b)) ? 1u : 0u))
65: #define BK7258_I2C1_FREQ_DIV(rate) \
66:   (BK7258_I2C1_ROUND_UP(BK7258_I2C1_ROUND_UP(BK7258_I2C1_XTAL_FREQ, (rate)) - 6u, 3u) - 1u)
67: 
68: /* Master-write state sequence, mirroring i2c_driver.c's
69:  * i2c_master_status_t (only the subset this write-only driver needs). */
70: enum bk7258_i2c1_state_e
71: {
72:   BK7258_I2C1_STATE_IDLE = 0,
73:   BK7258_I2C1_STATE_TX_DEV_ADDR,
74:   BK7258_I2C1_STATE_TX_REG_ADDR,
75:   BK7258_I2C1_STATE_TX_DATA,
76: };
77: 
78: static sem_t g_i2c1_done_sem;
79: static volatile enum bk7258_i2c1_state_e g_i2c1_state;
80: static volatile bool g_i2c1_ack_ok;
81: static uint8_t g_i2c1_dev_addr;
82: static uint8_t g_i2c1_reg_addr;
83: static uint8_t g_i2c1_data;
84: 
85: static void bk7258_i2c1_stop(void)
86: {
87:   /* Per i2c_ll_enable_stop()'s comment in the reference driver: sm_int
88:    * (bit[0]) and stop (bit[9]) must be written together in the same
89:    * write, otherwise the hardware will not actually issue a STOP
90:    * condition on the bus. */
91:   putreg32(BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_SM_INT | BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_STOP,
92:            BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
93:   g_i2c1_state = BK7258_I2C1_STATE_IDLE;
94: }
95: 
96: static int bk7258_i2c1_isr(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
97: {
98:   uint32_t int_status = getreg32(BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
99: 
100:   if ((int_status & BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_SM_INT) == 0)
101:     {
102:       /* Not the per-byte state-machine interrupt (e.g. scl_timeout,
103:        * arb_lost): clear whatever fired and bail out without touching
104:        * the write sequence, matching i2c1_isr_common()'s early return
105:        * for the same condition. */
106:       putreg32(int_status, BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
107:       return 0;
108:     }
109: 
110:   /* ack (bit[8]) reads as 1 when the previous byte was ACKed by the
111:    * slave, per i2c_ll_is_rx_ack_triggered()/i2c_ll_is_tx_ack_triggered()
112:    * both testing BIT(8) -- the same status bit serves both roles
113:    * depending on tx_mode, which master-write transactions always are. */
114:   bool acked = (int_status & BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_ACK) != 0;
115: 
116:   if (!acked)
117:     {
118:       g_i2c1_ack_ok = false;
119:       bk7258_i2c1_stop();
120:       nxsem_post(&g_i2c1_done_sem);
121:       /* Clear the interrupt (sm_int alone; no stop/start bit needed here
122:        * since bk7258_i2c1_stop() already issued its own combined
123:        * sm_int|stop write above). */
124:       putreg32(BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_SM_INT, BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
125:       return 0;
126:     }
127: 
128:   switch (g_i2c1_state)
129:     {
130:       case BK7258_I2C1_STATE_TX_DEV_ADDR:
131:         g_i2c1_state = BK7258_I2C1_STATE_TX_REG_ADDR;
132:         putreg32(g_i2c1_reg_addr & BK7258_I2C1_DATA_MASK,
133:                  BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_DATA);
134:         putreg32(BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_SM_INT, BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
135:         break;
136: 
137:       case BK7258_I2C1_STATE_TX_REG_ADDR:
138:         g_i2c1_state = BK7258_I2C1_STATE_TX_DATA;
139:         putreg32(g_i2c1_data & BK7258_I2C1_DATA_MASK,
140:                  BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_DATA);
141:         putreg32(BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_SM_INT, BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
142:         break;
143: 
144:       case BK7258_I2C1_STATE_TX_DATA:
145:         g_i2c1_ack_ok = true;
146:         bk7258_i2c1_stop();
147:         nxsem_post(&g_i2c1_done_sem);
148:         putreg32(BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_SM_INT, BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
149:         break;
150: 
151:       default:
152:         putreg32(int_status, BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
153:         break;
154:     }
155: 
156:   return 0;
157: }
158: 
159: void bk7258_i2c1_init(void)
160: {
161:   uint32_t freq_div = BK7258_I2C1_FREQ_DIV(BK7258_I2C1_BAUD_RATE);
162: 
163:   nxsem_init(&g_i2c1_done_sem, 0, 0);
164:   g_i2c1_state = BK7258_I2C1_STATE_IDLE;
165: 
166:   /* Enable the I2C1 *module* clock gate (BK_avdk_smp's
167:    * sys_drv_dev_clk_pwr_up(CLK_PWR_ID_I2C2, ...), called from
168:    * i2c_clock_enable(I2C_ID_1) in the reference i2c_driver.c).  This is
169:    * a separate, more fundamental gate than sm_bus_cfg.freq_div (the bus
170:    * baud-rate divider) or global_ctrl.clk_gate_bypass (an internal
171:    * ack-bit-visibility bypass): without this bit, the I2C1 block's
172:    * state machine receives no clock at all, so writing the start bit
173:    * in bk7258_i2c1_write_reg() is accepted by the register interface
174:    * (which is on a different, always-clocked bus) but never actually
175:    * advances the transaction -- sm_int never fires, indistinguishable
176:    * from a dead bus purely from register-level symptoms.  See
177:    * hardware/bk7258_sysctrl.h's BK7258_I2C1_MODULE_CLK_EN comment for
178:    * the register-map citation. */
179:   modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_DEVCLK_EN, 0, BK7258_I2C1_MODULE_CLK_EN);
180: 
181:   /* Route GPIO42/GPIO43 to the I2C1_SCL/I2C1_SDA hardware function.
182:    *
183:    * NOTE: bk7258_gpio_input_pullup() must NOT be called here (as an
184:    * earlier version of this driver did, attempting to also enable the
185:    * pins' internal pull-ups): it unconditionally clears
186:    * BK7258_GPIO_SECOND_FUNCTION (see bk7258_gpio.c), and
187:    * bk7258_gpio_set_function() unconditionally clears
188:    * BK7258_GPIO_PULL_ENABLE (see the same file) -- calling both back to
189:    * back, in either order, leaves one of "second function selected" or
190:    * "internal pull-up enabled" clobbered by the other's write.  This
191:    * board's schematic (sheet 4/6) already provides external 4.7K
192:    * pull-ups to VDDGPIO on both IIC1_SCL/IIC1_SDA nets, so the internal
193:    * pull-up is not required for correct bus operation; only the pinmux
194:    * function selection matters here. */
195:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(BK7258_I2C1_SCL_PIN, BK7258_I2C1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
196:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(BK7258_I2C1_SDA_PIN, BK7258_I2C1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
197: 
198:   /* Soft-reset then configure sm_bus_cfg, matching i2c_hal_init_instance()
199:    * (soft_reset=1, then zero sm_bus_cfg/sm_bus_status) followed by
200:    * i2c_hal_configure()'s field-by-field setup. */
201:   putreg32(BK7258_I2C1_SOFT_RESET, BK7258_I2C1_GLOBAL_CTRL);
202:   putreg32(0, BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_CFG);
203:   putreg32(0, BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS);
204: 
205:   putreg32((freq_div << BK7258_I2C1_CFG_FREQ_DIV_SHIFT) &
206:            BK7258_I2C1_CFG_FREQ_DIV_MASK,
207:            BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_CFG);
208: 
209:   /* idle_cr=0x3, scl_cr=0x4, clk_src=0x3, timeout_en=1, idle_det_en=1,
210:    * inh=0 (i2c_ll_enable_slave() clears inh to 0 even though this driver
211:    * never acts as a slave, matching i2c_hal_configure()'s call order:
212:    * enable_slave() runs after the cr/clk_src/timeout/idle_det writes). */
213:   modifyreg32(BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_CFG,
214:               BK7258_I2C1_CFG_IDLE_CR_MASK | BK7258_I2C1_CFG_SCL_CR_MASK |
215:               BK7258_I2C1_CFG_CLK_SRC_MASK,
216:               (0x3u << BK7258_I2C1_CFG_IDLE_CR_SHIFT) |
217:               (0x4u << BK7258_I2C1_CFG_SCL_CR_SHIFT) |
218:               (0x3u << BK7258_I2C1_CFG_CLK_SRC_SHIFT));
219:   modifyreg32(BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_CFG, BK7258_I2C1_CFG_INH,
220:               BK7258_I2C1_CFG_TIMEOUT_EN | BK7258_I2C1_CFG_IDLE_DET_EN);
221: 
222:   irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_I2C1, bk7258_i2c1_isr, NULL);
223:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_I2C1);
224: 
225:   /* Enable the peripheral (sm_bus_cfg.en=1), also bypassing the clock
226:    * gate so the ack bit is actually readable in the ISR -- per
227:    * i2c_ll_enable()'s comment: "need open clock bypass, otherwise cannot
228:    * read ack(BIT8) in i2c_isr". */
229:   putreg32(BK7258_I2C1_CLK_GATE_BYPASS, BK7258_I2C1_GLOBAL_CTRL);
230:   modifyreg32(BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_CFG, 0, BK7258_I2C1_CFG_EN);
231: }
232: 
233: bool bk7258_i2c1_write_reg(uint8_t i2c_addr, uint8_t reg, uint8_t value)
234: {
235:   irqstate_t flags;
236:   int ret;
237:   int busy_wait_us;
238: 
239:   /* Wait for the bus to report idle before issuing a new START,
240:    * matching i2c_hardware_memory_write_impl()'s
241:    * i2c_wait_sm_bus_idle() call.  sm_bus_status.busy (bit[15]) lives in
242:    * the same register as INT_STATUS (both are REG_0x05 per
243:    * i2c_struct.h's sm_bus_status union), so BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS is
244:    * read here rather than a separate "status" register.  Without this
245:    * check, if busy is stuck set (e.g. right after
246:    * bk7258_i2c1_init() enables the peripheral while the external bus
247:    * lines are still settling), writing the start bit below would be
248:    * silently ignored by the hardware state machine -- producing
249:    * exactly the "interrupt never fires, write_reg() times out"
250:    * symptom, indistinguishable from a dead/unwired bus without this
251:    * check to rule it out. */
252:   for (busy_wait_us = 0;
253:        (getreg32(BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS) &
254:         BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_BUSY) != 0 && busy_wait_us < 10000;
255:        busy_wait_us += 100)
256:     {
257:       up_udelay(100);
258:     }
259: 
260:   g_i2c1_dev_addr = i2c_addr;
261:   g_i2c1_reg_addr = reg;
262:   g_i2c1_data = value;
263:   g_i2c1_ack_ok = false;
264: 
265:   flags = enter_critical_section();
266: 
267:   /* Write the (7-bit addr << 1 | write-bit=0) byte first, then set
268:    * start=1, matching i2c_master_set_write_dev_addr()'s comment: "write
269:    * slave_addr first, then enable start bit, otherwise the slave_addr
270:    * written will be zero." */
271:   putreg32((uint32_t)(i2c_addr << 1) & BK7258_I2C1_DATA_MASK,
272:            BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_DATA);
273:   g_i2c1_state = BK7258_I2C1_STATE_TX_DEV_ADDR;
274:   modifyreg32(BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS, 0, BK7258_I2C1_STATUS_START);
275: 
276:   leave_critical_section(flags);
277: 
278:   /* Bounded wait: 100ms is generous for a 3-byte 100kHz transaction
279:    * (~270us of bus time) plus scheduling jitter, while still failing
280:    * fast if the slave never responds (e.g. wrong wiring) rather than
281:    * hanging board_late_initialize() indefinitely. */
282:   ret = nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible(&g_i2c1_done_sem, MSEC2TICK(100));
283:   if (ret < 0)
284:     {
285:       /* Timed out: the ISR never ran to completion (either the I2C1
286:        * interrupt never fired at all -- e.g. pinmux/clock
287:        * misconfiguration, or a hardware issue independent of ACK/NACK
288:        * -- or it fired but got stuck mid-sequence).  This is a
289:        * distinct failure mode from a clean NACK (which nxsem_post()s
290:        * promptly with g_i2c1_ack_ok=false) and is logged differently
291:        * here so board bring-up logs can tell "the bus electrically
292:        * never responded at all" apart from "the slave was reachable
293:        * and explicitly rejected". */
294:       printf("i2c1: write_reg(addr=0x%02x, reg=0x%02x) timed out "
295:              "waiting for the I2C1 interrupt (int_status=0x%08x, "
296:              "sm_bus_cfg=0x%08x) -- the ISR never completed the "
297:              "transaction\n",
298:              i2c_addr, reg, (unsigned int)getreg32(BK7258_I2C1_INT_STATUS),
299:              (unsigned int)getreg32(BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_CFG));
300: 
301:       /* Timed out: force the state machine back to idle so the next
302:        * write_reg() call starts clean, and disable+re-enable the
303:        * peripheral to clear any stuck bus condition, matching
304:        * i2c1_isr_common()'s SCL-timeout recovery path
305:        * (i2c_hal_disable() + i2c_hal_enable()). */
306:       g_i2c1_state = BK7258_I2C1_STATE_IDLE;
307:       modifyreg32(BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_CFG, BK7258_I2C1_CFG_EN, 0);
308:       modifyreg32(BK7258_I2C1_SM_BUS_CFG, 0, BK7258_I2C1_CFG_EN);
309:       return false;
310:     }
311: 
312:   if (!g_i2c1_ack_ok)
313:     {
314:       printf("i2c1: write_reg(addr=0x%02x, reg=0x%02x) got a clean "
315:              "NACK (the I2C1 interrupt fired and completed, but the "
316:              "slave never pulled ACK) -- the bus is electrically "
317:              "responsive, the device at this address is not\n",
318:              i2c_addr, reg);
319:     }
320: 
321:   return g_i2c1_ack_ok;
322: }

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_qspi.c
3:  *
4:  * BK7258 QSPI1 command-channel driver (no DMA, cmd_c/cmd_d indirect command
5:  * path only).  Register layout source: bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
6:  * ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/qspi_struct.h and hal/qspi_ll.h.  QSPI0
7:  * and QSPI1 are two identical controller instances differing only in base
8:  * address and which fixed GPIO group is wired to their CLK/CSN/IO0-3
9:  * signal lines.
10:  *
11:  * Corrected from QSPI0 to QSPI1 (2026-07-31): this driver originally
12:  * targeted QSPI0 (base 0x46040000, GPIO22/23/24/25) because that is the
13:  * pin group used by bk_avdk_smp's generic
14:  * projects/spi_lcd_example/qspi_lcd_example reference configs. Those
15:  * reference projects' own hardware wires their LCD to that pin group, but
16:  * this board's actual schematic
17:  * (AIDK_AI玩具开发板_原理图.pdf sheet 2/6 main chip pin table + sheet 5/6
18:  * CN5 single-screen connector) shows the panel's LCD_QSPI_CLK/CS/D0/D1 net
19:  * labels are wired to chip pins 35/34/33/32 = P2/P3/P4/P5 =
20:  * GPIO2/GPIO3/GPIO4/GPIO5, which per the chip's pinmux table
21:  * (bk_avdk_smp/ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_map.h GPIO_DEV_MAP)
22:  * carry QSPI1_CLK/QSPI1_CSN/QSPI1_IO0/QSPI1_IO1 (function-select index 6),
23:  * not QSPI0.  Symptom that led to this fix: with the QSPI0 assumption,
24:  * bk7258_qspi0_send_cmd() always timed out on the very first init command
25:  * (0xFE) -- GPIO22-25 were pinmuxed to QSPI0, but the panel is not
26:  * physically wired to those pins, so cmd_start_done never asserts and the
27:  * 10000-iteration wait always exhausts.  See
28:  * hardware/bk7258_memorymap.h's BK7258_QSPI1_BASE comment for the full
29:  * schematic evidence chain (chip pin numbers, net names, gpio_map.h
30:  * excerpt).
31:  *
32:  * Note the schematic's literal net names ("LCD_QSPI_D0" etc.) do NOT
33:  * match the SoC's real hardware role for these pins (CLK/CSN, not data
34:  * lines) -- PCB net labels are the board designer's arbitrary
35:  * connector-pin numbering convention, not a statement about which SoC
36:  * peripheral function is actually multiplexed onto that pad.  The real
37:  * role is only knowable from gpio_map.h's per-pin function array, which is
38:  * what this driver's pin/function assignments below are built from.
39:  *
40:  * Register offsets (byte offset from BK7258_QSPI1_BASE, word index in
41:  * qspi_hw_t from qspi_struct.h in parentheses) -- identical layout to
42:  * QSPI0, only the base address differs:
43:  *   glb_ctrl    0x08 (REG_0x02) - bit[0] soft_reset, bit[1] bps_clkgate
44:  *   cmd_c_l     0x40 (REG_0x10)
45:  *   cmd_c_h     0x44 (REG_0x11)
46:  *   cmd_c_cfg1  0x48 (REG_0x12)
47:  *   cmd_c_cfg2  0x4c (REG_0x13) - bit[0] cmd_start
48:  *   cmd_d_l     0x50 (REG_0x14)
49:  *   cmd_d_h     0x54 (REG_0x15)
50:  *   cmd_d_cfg1  0x58 (REG_0x16)
51:  *   cmd_d_cfg2  0x5c (REG_0x17) - bit[0] cmd_start
52:  *   status      0x70 (REG_0x1c) - bit[2] cmd_start_done
53:  *   status_clr  0x6c (REG_0x1b) - bit[2] clr_cmd_start_done
54:  *
55:  * The "command done" flag is carried by the status register's
56:  * cmd_start_done bit, not by core_status (REG_0x03, byte offset 0x0c),
57:  * which is an unused, un-bitfielded raw word in the vendor headers and is
58:  * never read by qspi_ll_is_cmd_start_done()/qspi_ll_wait_cmd_done().  The
59:  * start trigger is not a separate register either: it is the cmd_start bit
60:  * inside each channel's own cfg2 register (cmd_c_cfg2 for the send path,
61:  * cmd_d_cfg2 for the read path), matching qspi_ll_cmd_c_start() and
62:  * qspi_ll_cmd_d_start().
63:  *
64:  * Pinmux: the QSPI1 controller's four signal lines (CLK/CSN/IO0/IO1) are
65:  * shared, multiplexed GPIO pads (GPIO_2/3/4/5 on this SoC), not dedicated
66:  * pins.  Each pad defaults to plain GPIO after reset and must be switched
67:  * to QSPI1 mode via the "second function" pinmux mechanism before the
68:  * controller's TX/RX lines are actually connected to the pad -- without
69:  * this step cmd_start_done never asserts because the panel never receives
70:  * the command.  Source of the function-select index (6) for QSPI1 on
71:  * GPIO_2/3/4/5: bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
72:  * ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/gpio_map.h gpio_map_table (QSPI1_CLK/
73:  * CSN/IO0/IO1 are the 7th entry, index 6, in each pin's per-function
74:  * array).  The pinmux register plumbing itself (BK7258_GPIO_SYS_BASE etc.)
75:  * is shared with bk7258_gpio.c; see bk7258_gpio_set_function().
76:  *
77:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
78:  ****************************************************************************/
79: 
80: #include <nuttx/config.h>
81: #include <nuttx/arch.h>
82: #include <stdbool.h>
83: #include <stdint.h>
84: 
85: #include "arm_internal.h"
86: #include "hardware/bk7258_memorymap.h"
87: #include "hardware/bk7258_sysctrl.h"
88: #include "bk7258_gpio.h"
89: #include "bk7258_qspi.h"
90: 
91: #define QSPI1_CLK_PIN               2u
92: #define QSPI1_CSN_PIN               3u
93: #define QSPI1_IO0_PIN               4u
94: #define QSPI1_IO1_PIN               5u
95: #define QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION       6u
96: 
97: #define QSPI_REG(offset)           (BK7258_QSPI1_BASE + (offset))
98: 
99: #define QSPI_GLB_CTRL              QSPI_REG(0x08u)
100: #define QSPI_GLB_CTRL_SOFT_RESET   (1u << 0)
101: 
102: #define QSPI_CMD_C_L               QSPI_REG(0x40u)
103: #define QSPI_CMD_C_H               QSPI_REG(0x44u)
104: #define QSPI_CMD_C_CFG1            QSPI_REG(0x48u)
105: #define QSPI_CMD_C_CFG2            QSPI_REG(0x4cu)
106: 
107: #define QSPI_CMD_D_L               QSPI_REG(0x50u)
108: #define QSPI_CMD_D_H               QSPI_REG(0x54u)
109: #define QSPI_CMD_D_CFG1            QSPI_REG(0x58u)
110: #define QSPI_CMD_D_CFG2            QSPI_REG(0x5cu)
111: 
112: #define QSPI_STATUS                QSPI_REG(0x70u)
113: #define QSPI_STATUS_CMD_START_DONE (1u << 2)
114: 
115: #define QSPI_STATUS_CLR                 QSPI_REG(0x6cu)
116: #define QSPI_STATUS_CLR_CMD_START_DONE  (1u << 2)
117: 
118: #define QSPI_CMD_START_BIT         (1u << 0)
119: 
120: /* Matches qspi_ll_wait_cmd_done()'s 10000-iteration bound
121:  * (ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/qspi_ll.h) instead of looping forever,
122:  * so a pinmux or wiring problem produces a diagnosable timeout rather than
123:  * an unrecoverable hang. */
124: #define QSPI_WAIT_DONE_MAX_ITER    10000
125: 
126: static bool bk7258_qspi0_wait_done(void)
127: {
128:   int i;
129: 
130:   for (i = 0; i < QSPI_WAIT_DONE_MAX_ITER; i++)
131:     {
132:       if ((getreg32(QSPI_STATUS) & QSPI_STATUS_CMD_START_DONE) != 0)
133:         {
134:           break;
135:         }
136: 
137:       up_udelay(1);
138:     }
139: 
140:   /* Clear cmd_start_done (write 1 then 0), matching qspi_ll_wait_cmd_done()
141:    * -- required so a stale "done" flag from this command does not make
142:    * the next command's wait loop return immediately without having
143:    * actually completed. */
144:   modifyreg32(QSPI_STATUS_CLR, 0, QSPI_STATUS_CLR_CMD_START_DONE);
145:   modifyreg32(QSPI_STATUS_CLR, QSPI_STATUS_CLR_CMD_START_DONE, 0);
146: 
147:   return i < QSPI_WAIT_DONE_MAX_ITER;
148: }
149: 
150: void bk7258_qspi0_init(void)
151: {
152:   /* Enable the QSPI1 *module* clock gate first, matching
153:    * qspi_id_init_common()'s documented call order ("1. set clock, 2. set
154:    * gpio as qspi, 3. enable interrupt") in bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
155:    * ap/middleware/driver/qspi/qspi_driver.c.  Without this bit, register
156:    * writes to the QSPI1 block are accepted (no bus fault) but the
157:    * controller's internal command state machine has no clock to run on,
158:    * so cmd_start_done never asserts -- see
159:    * hardware/bk7258_sysctrl.h's BK7258_QSPI1_MODULE_CLK_EN comment for
160:    * the register-map citation and the I2C1 precedent this is modeled
161:    * after. */
162:   modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_DEVCLK_EN, 0, BK7258_QSPI1_MODULE_CLK_EN);
163: 
164:   /* Switch the 4 shared GPIO pads to QSPI1 mode before touching the
165:    * controller; see file header comment for why this is required and why
166:    * it is QSPI1 (GPIO2-5) rather than QSPI0 (GPIO22-25) on this board. */
167:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(QSPI1_CLK_PIN, QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
168:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(QSPI1_CSN_PIN, QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
169:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(QSPI1_IO0_PIN, QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
170:   bk7258_gpio_set_function(QSPI1_IO1_PIN, QSPI1_PINMUX_FUNCTION);
171: 
172:   putreg32(QSPI_GLB_CTRL_SOFT_RESET, QSPI_GLB_CTRL);
173:   up_udelay(10);
174:   putreg32(0, QSPI_GLB_CTRL);
175: }
176: 
177: bool bk7258_qspi0_send_cmd(uint8_t cmd, const uint8_t *data, uint8_t data_len)
178: {
179:   uint32_t cmd_c_h = (uint32_t)cmd;
180:   uint32_t cmd_c_l = 0;
181:   uint8_t i;
182: 
183:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_C_L);
184:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_C_H);
185:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_C_CFG1);
186:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_C_CFG2);
187: 
188:   if (data_len > 0 && data_len <= 4)
189:     {
190:       for (i = 0; i < data_len; i++)
191:         {
192:           cmd_c_l |= ((uint32_t)data[i]) << (i * 8);
193:         }
194: 
195:       putreg32(cmd_c_l, QSPI_CMD_C_L);
196:     }
197: 
198:   putreg32(cmd_c_h, QSPI_CMD_C_H);
199:   modifyreg32(QSPI_CMD_C_CFG2, 0, QSPI_CMD_START_BIT);
200:   return bk7258_qspi0_wait_done();
201: }
202: 
203: uint32_t bk7258_qspi0_read_id(void)
204: {
205:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_D_L);
206:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_D_H);
207:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_D_CFG1);
208:   putreg32(0, QSPI_CMD_D_CFG2);
209: 
210:   putreg32(0x04u, QSPI_CMD_D_H); /* GC9D01 read-ID opcode, single byte cmd */
211:   modifyreg32(QSPI_CMD_D_CFG2, 0, QSPI_CMD_START_BIT);
212:   (void)bk7258_qspi0_wait_done();
213: 
214:   return getreg32(QSPI_CMD_D_L);
215: }

(End of file - total 215 lines)

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_yuv_buf.c
3:  *
4:  * BK7258 YUV_BUF controller thin port, YUV direct-capture mode only.
5:  * Register layout source: bk_avdk_smp release/v3.1.1
6:  * ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/soc/yuv_buf_struct.h and
7:  * ap/middleware/soc/bk7258_ap/hal/yuv_buf_ll.h.
8:  *
9:  * Register offsets (byte offset from BK7258_YUV_BUF_BASE, word index in
10:  * yuv_buf_hw_t from yuv_buf_struct.h in parentheses):
11:  *   global_ctrl  0x08 (REG_0x02) - bit[0] soft_reset, bit[1] clk_gate_bypass
12:  *   ctrl         0x10 (REG_0x04) - bit[0] yuv_mode, bit[12] h264_mode
13:  *   pixel        0x14 (REG_0x05) - bit[0:7] x_pixel, bit[8:15] y_pixel,
14:  *                                  bit[16:31] frame_blk
15:  *   em_base_addr 0x20 (REG_0x08)
16:  *   int_en       0x24 (REG_0x09) - bit[1] yuv_arv_int_en, bit[2]

28:  * width/height as its parameters.  frame_blk = x_pixel * y_pixel / 2
29:  * (using the already-/8 x_pixel/y_pixel values).

31:  * PSRAM line buffer: YUV direct-capture mode hard-codes
32:  * em_base_addr/emr_base_addr to SOC_PSRAM_DATA_BASE

48:  * a 640x480 frame) is NOT implemented in this file -- this driver only
49:  * reports which ping-pong bank (SM0/SM1) fired, per batch, via

51:  * each batch out via DMA before the hardware overwrites that bank with
52:  * the next occurrence, and detecting frame completion is the caller's

89: #define YUV_BUF_INT_EN_SM1_WR      (1u << 3)
90:

93: #define YUV_BUF_INT_STATUS_SM1_WR  (1u << 3)

104: static int bk7258_yuv_buf_isr(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
105: {
106:   uint32_t status = getreg32(YUV_BUF_INT_STATUS);
107: 
108:   /* Write-1-to-clear: write back exactly the bits that were read as set,
109:    * per yuv_buf_ll_clear_interrupt_status(). */
110:   putreg32(status, YUV_BUF_INT_STATUS);
111: 
112:   /* SM0_WR and SM1_WR are reported as separate bits and, per the
113:    * hardware's alternating ping-pong behavior, are not expected to both
114:    * be set in the same status read; handle them independently rather
115:    * than assuming mutual exclusion, so a spurious simultaneous report
116:    * (if it ever occurs) still drains both banks instead of silently
117:    * dropping one. */
118:   if (g_line_cb != NULL)

121:         {

123:         }
124: 
125:       if ((status & YUV_BUF_INT_STATUS_SM1_WR) != 0)
126:         {
127:           g_line_cb(BK7258_YUV_BUF_BANK_SM1, g_line_cb_arg);
128:         }
129:     }
130: 
131:   return 0;
132: }

138:   putreg32(0, YUV_BUF_GLOBAL_CTRL);

144: void bk7258_yuv_buf_configure(uint16_t width, uint16_t height)
145: {
146:   uint32_t x_pixel = width / 8u;
147:   uint32_t y_pixel = height / 8u;
148:   uint32_t frame_blk = (x_pixel * y_pixel) / 2u;
149:   uint32_t pixel_reg;

151:   /* One ping-pong bank holds 8 lines of YUV422 (2 bytes/pixel) data,
152:    * matching bk_dvp.c's "yuv_config.yuv_pingpong_length = config->width
153:    * * 8 * 2".  Saved here so bk7258_yuv_buf_get_line_batch_bytes() can
154:    * report it without callers needing to duplicate this formula. */
155:   g_line_batch_bytes = (uint32_t)width * 8u * 2u;

157:   pixel_reg = (x_pixel << YUV_BUF_PIXEL_X_SHIFT) |
158:               (y_pixel << YUV_BUF_PIXEL_Y_SHIFT) |
159:               (frame_blk << YUV_BUF_PIXEL_FRAME_BLK_SHIFT);
160:   putreg32(pixel_reg, YUV_BUF_PIXEL);

79:  * Description:

82: 
83: static void fifo_drain(void)
84: {
85:   putreg32(0, RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST);
86: 
87:   while (getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST) & RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST_VLD)
88:     {
89:       getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_RD);
90:     }
91: 
92:   __asm__ volatile ("sev");
93: }

95: /****************************************************************************
96:  * Name: fifo_comm
97:  *
98:  * Description:
99:  *   Communicate with CPU Core 1 using inter-processor FIFO for boot
100:  *
101:  * Input Parameters:
102:  *   msg - Data to be sent to Core 1
103:  *
104:  * Returned Value:
105:  *   true on success; false on failure.
106:  *
107:  ****************************************************************************/
108: 
109: static int fifo_comm(uint32_t msg)
110: {
111:   uint32_t rcv;
112: 
113:   while (!(getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST) & RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST_RDY))
114:     ;
115:   putreg32(msg, RP2040_SIO_FIFO_WR);
116:   __asm__ volatile ("sev");
117: 
118:   while (!(getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST) & RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST_VLD))
119:     __asm__ volatile ("wfe");
120: 
121:   rcv = getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_RD);
122: 
123:   return msg == rcv;
124: }

174: /****************************************************************************
175:  * Name: up_cpu_start
176:  *
177:  * Description:
178:  *   In an SMP configuration, only one CPU is initially active (CPU 0).
179:  *   System initialization occurs on that single thread. At the completion of
180:  *   the initialization of the OS, just before beginning normal multitasking,
181:  *   the additional CPUs would be started by calling this function.
182:  *
183:  *   Each CPU is provided the entry point to its IDLE task when started.  A
184:  *   TCB for each CPU's IDLE task has been initialized and placed in the
185:  *   CPU's g_assignedtasks[cpu] list.  No stack has been allocated or
186:  *   initialized.
187:  *
188:  *   The OS initialization logic calls this function repeatedly until each
189:  *   CPU has been started, 1 through (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS-1).
190:  *
191:  * Input Parameters:
192:  *   cpu - The index of the CPU being started.  This will be a numeric
193:  *         value in the range of one to (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS-1).
194:  *         (CPU 0 is already active)
195:  *
196:  * Returned Value:
197:  *   Zero on success; a negated errno value on failure.
198:  *
199:  ****************************************************************************/

201: int up_cpu_start(int cpu)
202: {

204:   struct tcb_s *tcb = current_task(cpu);
205:   uint32_t core1_boot_msg[5];
206: 
207:   DPRINTF("cpu=%d\n", cpu);
208: 
209: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_INSTRUMENTATION
210:   /* Notify of the start event */
211: 
212:   sched_note_cpu_start(this_task(), cpu);
213: #endif
214: 
215:   /* Reset Core 1 */
216: 
217:   setbits_reg32(RP2040_PSM_PROC1, RP2040_PSM_FRCE_OFF);
218:   while (!(getreg32(RP2040_PSM_FRCE_OFF) & RP2040_PSM_PROC1))
219:     ;
220:   clrbits_reg32(RP2040_PSM_PROC1, RP2040_PSM_FRCE_OFF);
221: 
222:   spin_lock(&g_core1_boot);
223:

225:

227:   core1_boot_msg[1] = 1;
228:   core1_boot_msg[2] = getreg32(ARMV6M_SYSCON_VECTAB);
229:   core1_boot_msg[3] = (uint32_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr +
230:                                 tcb->adj_stack_size;
231:   core1_boot_msg[4] = (uint32_t)core1_boot;

233:   do

235:       fifo_drain();
236:       for (i = 0; i < 5; i++)

252:

254:

40: /****************************************************************************
41:  * Name: up_cpu_idlestack
42:  *
43:  * Description:
44:  *   Allocate a stack for the CPU[n] IDLE task (n > 0) if appropriate and
45:  *   setup up stack-related information in the IDLE task's TCB.  This
46:  *   function is always called before up_cpu_start().  This function is
47:  *   only called for the CPU's initial IDLE task; up_create_task is used for
48:  *   all normal tasks, pthreads, and kernel threads for all CPUs.
49:  *
50:  *   The initial IDLE task is a special case because the CPUs can be started
51:  *   in different wans in different environments:
52:  *
53:  *   1. The CPU may already have been started and waiting in a low power
54:  *      state for up_cpu_start().  In this case, the IDLE thread's stack
55:  *      has already been allocated and is already in use.  Here
56:  *      up_cpu_idlestack() only has to provide information about the
57:  *      already allocated stack.
58:  *
59:  *   2. The CPU may be disabled but started when up_cpu_start() is called.
60:  *      In this case, a new stack will need to be created for the IDLE
61:  *      thread and this function is then equivalent to:
62:  *
63:  *      return up_create_stack(tcb, stack_size, TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_KERNEL);
64:  *
65:  *   The following TCB fields must be initialized by this function:
66:  *
67:  *   - adj_stack_size: Stack size after adjustment for hardware, processor,
68:  *     etc.  This value is retained only for debug purposes.
69:  *   - stack_alloc_ptr: Pointer to allocated stack
70:  *   - stack_base_ptr: Adjusted stack base pointer after the TLS Data and
71:  *     Arguments has been removed from the stack allocation.
72:  *
73:  * Input Parameters:
74:  *   - cpu:         CPU index that indicates which CPU the IDLE task is
75:  *                  being created for.
76:  *   - tcb:         The TCB of new CPU IDLE task
77:  *   - stack_size:  The requested stack size for the IDLE task.  At least
78:  *                  this much must be allocated.  This should be
79:  *                  CONFIG_SMP_STACK_SIZE.
80:  *
81:  ****************************************************************************/
82: 
83: int up_cpu_idlestack(int cpu, struct tcb_s *tcb, size_t stack_size)
84: {
85: #if CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS > 1
86:   up_create_stack(tcb, stack_size, TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_KERNEL);
87: #endif
88:   return OK;
89: }
90: 
91: #endif /* CONFIG_SMP */

53: /****************************************************************************
54:  * Name: rp2040_handle_irqreq
55:  *
56:  * Description:
57:  *   If an irq handling request is found on cpu, call up_enable_irq() or
58:  *   up_disable_irq().
59:  *
60:  * Input Parameters:
61:  *   irqreq - The IRQ number to be handled (>0 : enable / <0 : disable)
62:  *
63:  ****************************************************************************/
64: 
65: static void rp2040_handle_irqreq(int irqreq)
66: {
67:   DEBUGASSERT(this_cpu() == 0);
68: 
69:   if (irqreq > 0)
70:     {
71:       up_enable_irq(irqreq);
72:     }
73:   else
74:     {
75:       up_disable_irq(-irqreq);
76:     }
77: }
78:

82: 
83: /****************************************************************************
84:  * Name: rp2040_smp_call_handler
85:  *
86:  * Description:
87:  *   This is the handler for SMP_CALL.
88:  *
89:  ****************************************************************************/
90: 
91: int rp2040_smp_call_handler(int irq, void *c, void *arg)
92: {
93:   int cpu = this_cpu();
94:   int irqreq;
95:   uint32_t stat;
96: 
97:   nxsched_smp_call_handler(irq, c, arg);
98: 
99:   stat = getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST);
100:   if (stat & (RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST_ROE | RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST_WOF))
101:     {
102:       /* Clear sticky flag */
103: 
104:       putreg32(0, RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST);
105:     }
106: 
107:   if (!(stat & RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST_VLD))
108:     {
109:       /* No data received */
110: 
111:       return OK;
112:     }
113: 
114:   irqreq = getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_RD);
115: 
116:   if (irqreq != 0)
117:     {
118:       /* Handle IRQ enable/disable request */
119: 
120:       rp2040_handle_irqreq(irqreq);
121:       return OK;
122:     }
123: 
124:   DPRINTF("cpu%d will be paused\n", cpu);
125: 
126:   nxsched_process_delivered(cpu);
127: 
128:   return OK;
129: }
130: 
131: /****************************************************************************
132:  * Name: up_send_smp_sched
133:  *
134:  * Description:
135:  *   pause task execution on the CPU
136:  *   check whether there are tasks delivered to specified cpu
137:  *   and try to run them.
138:  *
139:  * Input Parameters:
140:  *   cpu - The index of the CPU to be paused.
141:  *
142:  * Returned Value:
143:  *   Zero on success; a negated errno value on failure.
144:  *
145:  * Assumptions:
146:  *   Called from within a critical section;
147:  *
148:  ****************************************************************************/
149: 
150: int up_send_smp_sched(int cpu)
151: {
152:   /* Generate IRQ for CPU(cpu) */
153: 
154:   while (!(getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST) & RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST_RDY))
155:     ;
156:   putreg32(0, RP2040_SIO_FIFO_WR);
157: 
158:   return OK;
159: }
160: 
161: /****************************************************************************
162:  * Name: up_send_smp_call
163:  *
164:  * Description:
165:  *   Send smp call to target cpu.
166:  *
167:  * Input Parameters:
168:  *   cpuset - The set of CPUs to receive the SGI.
169:  *
170:  * Returned Value:
171:  *   None.
172:  *
173:  ****************************************************************************/
174: 
175: void up_send_smp_call(cpu_set_t cpuset)
176: {
177:   int cpu;
178: 
179:   for (; cpuset != 0; cpuset &= ~(1 << cpu))
180:     {
181:       cpu = ffs(cpuset) - 1;
182:       up_send_smp_sched(cpu);
183:     }
184: }
185: 
186: /****************************************************************************
187:  * Name: rp2040_send_irqreq()
188:  *
189:  * Description:
190:  *   Send up_enable_irq() / up_disable_irq() request to the Core #0
191:  *
192:  *   This function is called from up_enable_irq() or up_disable_irq()
193:  *   to be handled on specified CPU. Locking protocol in the sequence is
194:  *   the same as up_pause_cpu() plus up_resume_cpu().
195:  *
196:  * Input Parameters:
197:  *   irqreq - The IRQ number to be handled (>0 : enable / <0 : disable)
198:  *
199:  ****************************************************************************/
200: 
201: void rp2040_send_irqreq(int irqreq)
202: {
203:   /* Send IRQ number to Core #0 */
204: 
205:   while (!(getreg32(RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST) & RP2040_SIO_FIFO_ST_RDY))
206:     ;
207:   putreg32(irqreq, RP2040_SIO_FIFO_WR);
208: }

191: noinline_function void arm_initialize_stack(void)
192: {
193:   uint32_t stacklim = up_get_intstackbase(this_cpu());
194:   uint32_t stack = stacklim + INTSTACK_SIZE;
195:   uint32_t temp = 0;
196: 
197:   __asm__ __volatile__
198:     (
199:       "mrs %1, CONTROL\n"
200:       "tst %1, #2\n"
201:       "bne 1f\n"
202: 
203:       /* Initialize PSP */
204: 
205:       "mrs %1, msp\n"
206:       "msr psp, %1\n"
207: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
208:       "mrs %1, msplim\n"
209:       "msr psplim, %1\n"
210: #else
211:       "mov %1, #0\n"
212:       "msr psplim, %1\n"
213: #endif
214:       "isb sy\n"
215: 
216:       /* Select PSP */
217: 
218:       "mrs %1, CONTROL\n"
219:       "orr %1, #2\n"
220:       "msr CONTROL, %1\n"
221:       "isb sy\n"
222: 
223:       /* Initialize MSP */
224: 
225:       "1:\n"
226:       "msr msp, %0\n"
227: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
228:       "msr msplim, %2\n"
229: #else

233:       "isb sy\n"
234:       :
235: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE

237: #else

128: /****************************************************************************
129:  * Name: up_cpu_start
130:  *
131:  * Description:
132:  *   In an SMP configuration, only one CPU is initially active (CPU 0).
133:  *   System initialization occurs on that single thread. At the completion of
134:  *   the initialization of the OS, just before beginning normal multitasking,
135:  *   the additional CPUs would be started by calling this function.
136:  *
137:  *   Each CPU is provided the entry point to its IDLE task when started.  A
138:  *   TCB for each CPU's IDLE task has been initialized and placed in the
139:  *   CPU's g_assignedtasks[cpu] list.  No stack has been allocated or
140:  *   initialized.
141:  *
142:  *   The OS initialization logic calls this function repeatedly until each
143:  *   CPU has been started, 1 through (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS-1).
144:  *
145:  * Input Parameters:
146:  *   cpu - The index of the CPU being started.  This will be a numeric
147:  *         value in the range of one to (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS-1).
148:  *         (CPU 0 is already active)
149:  *
150:  * Returned Value:
151:  *   Zero on success; a negated errno value on failure.
152:  *
153:  ****************************************************************************/
154: 
155: int up_cpu_start(int cpu)
156: {
157:   struct tcb_s *tcb = current_task(cpu);
158: 
159:   DPRINTF("cpu=%d\n", cpu);
160: 
161:   if (cpu != 1)
162:     {
163:       return -EINVAL;
164:     }
165: 
166: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_INSTRUMENTATION
167:   /* Notify of the start event */
168: 
169:   sched_note_cpu_start(this_task(), cpu);
170: #endif
171: 
172:   /* Reset coprocessor */
173: 
174:   putreg32(0x5a000000, SAM_RSTC_CPMR);
175: 
176:   /* Enable Coprocessor Bus Master Clock (write-only) */
177: 
178:   putreg32(PMC_CPKEY | PMC_CPBMCK, SAM_PMC_SCER);
179: 
180:   /* Enable Coprocessor Clock (write-only) */
181: 
182:   putreg32(PMC_CPKEY | PMC_CPCK, SAM_PMC_SCER);
183: 
184:   /* Set Coprocessor Clock Prescalar */
185: 
186:   modifyreg32(SAM_PMC_MCKR, PMC_MCKR_CPPRES_MASK, 0);
187: 
188:   /* Set Coprocessor Clock Source */
189: 
190:   modifyreg32(SAM_PMC_MCKR, PMC_MCKR_CPCSS_MASK, PMC_MCKR_CPCSS_PLLB);
191: 
192:   /* Unreset coprocessor pheripheral */
193: 
194:   putreg32(0x5a000010, SAM_RSTC_CPMR);
195: 
196:   /* Enable clock for SRAM1 where CPU1 starts (write-only) */
197: 
198:   putreg32(PMC_PID42, SAM_PMC_PCER1);
199: 
200:   /* Clear SRAM1 */
201: 
202:   memset((void *)SAM_INTSRAM1_BASE, 0, 16 * 1024);
203: 
204:   /* Copy initial vectors for CPU1 */
205: 
206:   putreg32((uint32_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr +
207:                      tcb->adj_stack_size, CPU1_VECTOR_ISTACK);
208:   putreg32((uint32_t)cpu1_boot, CPU1_VECTOR_RESETV);
209: 
210:   spin_lock(&g_cpu1_boot);
211: 
212:   /* Unreset coprocessor */
213: 
214:   putreg32(0x5a000011, SAM_RSTC_CPMR);
215: 
216:   /* IRQ setup CPU1->CPU0 */
217: 
218:   sam_ipc0_enableclk();
219:   putreg32(0x1, SAM_IPC0_ICCR); /* clear : write-only */
220:   putreg32(0x1, SAM_IPC0_IECR); /* enable : write-only */
221:   irq_attach(SAM_IRQ_SMP_CALL0, sam4cm_smp_call_handler, NULL);

224:   spin_lock(&g_cpu1_boot);
225:

71:  * Name: up_cpu_idlestack
72:  *
73:  * Description:
74:  *   Allocate a stack for the CPU[n] IDLE task (n > 0) if appropriate and
75:  *   setup up stack-related information in the IDLE task's TCB.  This
76:  *   function is always called before up_cpu_start().  This function is
77:  *   only called for the CPU's initial IDLE task; up_create_task is used for
78:  *   all normal tasks, pthreads, and kernel threads for all CPUs.
79:  *
80:  *   The initial IDLE task is a special case because the CPUs can be started
81:  *   in different wans in different environments:
82:  *
83:  *   1. The CPU may already have been started and waiting in a low power
84:  *      state for up_cpu_start().  In this case, the IDLE thread's stack
85:  *      has already been allocated and is already in use.  Here
86:  *      up_cpu_idlestack() only has to provide information about the
87:  *      already allocated stack.
88:  *
89:  *   2. The CPU may be disabled but started when up_cpu_start() is called.
90:  *      In this case, a new stack will need to be created for the IDLE
91:  *      thread and this function is then equivalent to:
92:  *
93:  *      return up_create_stack(tcb, stack_size, TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_KERNEL);
94:  *
95:  *   The following TCB fields must be initialized by this function:
96:  *
97:  *   - adj_stack_size: Stack size after adjustment for hardware, processor,
98:  *     etc.  This value is retained only for debug purposes.
99:  *   - stack_alloc_ptr: Pointer to allocated stack
100:  *   - stack_base_ptr: Adjusted stack base pointer after the TLS Data and
101:  *     Arguments has been removed from the stack allocation.
102:  *
103:  * Input Parameters:

105:  *                  being created for.
106:  *   - tcb:         The TCB of new CPU IDLE task
107:  *   - stack_size:  The requested stack size for the IDLE task.  At least
108:  *                  this much must be allocated.  This should be
109:  *                  CONFIG_SMP_STACK_SIZE.
110:  *
111:  ****************************************************************************/
112: 
113: int up_cpu_idlestack(int cpu, struct tcb_s *tcb, size_t stack_size)
114: {

116:   up_create_stack(tcb, stack_size, TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_KERNEL);

43:  * Description:
44:  *   Allocate a stack for the CPU[n] IDLE task (n > 0) if appropriate and
45:  *   setup up stack-related information in the IDLE task's TCB.  This
46:  *   function is always called before up_cpu_start().  This function is
47:  *   only called for the CPU's initial IDLE task; up_create_task is used for
48:  *   all normal tasks, pthreads, and kernel threads for all CPUs.
49:  *
50:  *   The initial IDLE task is a special case because the CPUs can be started
51:  *   in different wans in different environments:
52:  *
53:  *   1. The CPU may already have been started and waiting in a low power
54:  *      state for up_cpu_start().  In this case, the IDLE thread's stack
55:  *      has already been allocated and is already in use.  Here
56:  *      up_cpu_idlestack() only has to provide information about the
57:  *      already allocated stack.
58:  *
59:  *   2. The CPU may be disabled but started when up_cpu_start() is called.
60:  *      In this case, a new stack will need to be created for the IDLE
61:  *      thread and this function is then equivalent to:
62:  *
63:  *      return up_create_stack(tcb, stack_size, TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_KERNEL);
64:  *
65:  *   The following TCB fields must be initialized by this function:
66:  *
67:  *   - adj_stack_size: Stack size after adjustment for hardware, processor,
68:  *     etc.  This value is retained only for debug purposes.
69:  *   - stack_alloc_ptr: Pointer to allocated stack
70:  *   - stack_base_ptr: Adjusted stack base pointer after the TLS Data and
71:  *     Arguments has been removed from the stack allocation.
72:  *
73:  * Input Parameters:

81:  ****************************************************************************/

219: static void mb_ipc_task( void *para )
220: {
221: 	bk_err_t	ret_val;
222: 	u32    events;
223: 	u32    check_time = BEKEN_WAIT_FOREVER;
224: 
225: 	mb_ipc_init_lv_callback();
226: 
227: 	ret_val = rtos_init_event_ex(&mb_ipc_heart_event);
228: 
229: 	if(ret_val != BK_OK)
230: 	{
231: 		rtos_delete_thread(NULL);
232: 		return;
233: 	}
234: 
235: 	while(1)
236: 	{
237: 		events = rtos_wait_event_ex(&mb_ipc_heart_event, MB_IPC_ALL_FLAGS, true, check_time);
238: 
239: 		if(events == 0)
240: 		{
241: 			// timeout, so check heartbeat.
242: 			events = MB_IPC_HEARTBEAT_FLAG;
243: 		}
244: 
245: 		if(events & MB_IPC_STOP_CORE_FLAG)  // process this event at first!!!!
246: 		{
247: 			if(cpu_x_state == CORE_POWER_OFF)
248: 			{
249: 				events = 0;  // clear all events.
250: 			}
251: 		}
252: 
253: 		if(events & MB_IPC_START_CORE_FLAG)
254: 		{
255: 			u8   retry_cnt = 0;
256: 
257: 			while(cpu_x_state == CORE_STARTING)
258: 			{
259: 				ipc_heartbeat_timeout();
260: 
261: 				if(events & MB_IPC_POWER_UP_FLAG)
262: 				{
263: 					if(cpu_x_state == CORE_STARTING)
264: 					{
265: 						cpu_x_state = CORE_POWER_ON;
266: 						break;  // cpu1 power on.
267: 					}
268: 				}
269: 				else
270: 				{
271: 					if( retry_cnt > 3)
272: 					{
273: 						BK_DUMP_OUT("IPC retry to start core%d, retry_cnt:%d\r\n", cpu_x_id, retry_cnt);
274: 						// restart_cpu_x();
275: 						break;
276: 					}
277: 					else
278: 					{
279: 						events = rtos_wait_event_ex(&mb_ipc_heart_event, MB_IPC_POWER_UP_FLAG, true, 2000);//2s
280: 					}
281: 				}
282: 
283: 				retry_cnt++;
284: 			}
285: 
286: 			// discard this event when not in CORE_STARTING state.
287: 		}
288: 
289: 		if(events & MB_IPC_HEARTBEAT_FLAG)
290: 		{
291: 			if(ipc_heartbeat_timeout())
292: 			{
293: 				BK_LOGE(MOD_TAG, "IPC[%d]heartbeat timeout %d,%d\r\n",cpu_x_id,cpu_x_heartbeat_timestamp,(u32)rtos_get_time());
294: 				/*when cpu1 heartbeat timeout, then system reboot*/
295: 				cpu_x_heartbeat_timeout = 1;
296: 				ap_console_bridge_link_down();
297: 				BK_ASSERT(false);
298: 			}
299: 		}
300: 
301: 		if(cpu_x_state == CORE_POWER_OFF)
302: 		{
303: 			check_time = BEKEN_WAIT_FOREVER;
304: 		}
305: 		else
306: 		{
307: 			check_time = HB_TIMEOUT_MS;
308: 		}
309: 	}
310: }

有一处需要精确表述：`enter_critical_section()` 在 SMP 配置下会通过 NuttX scheduler recursive spinlock 提供跨核保护，而直接调用 `up_irq_save()` 仍只屏蔽本核中断。因此 GPIO/PWM 中使用前者并非天然失效，但它们会依赖 BK7258 atomic/spinlock backend 正确；Mailbox/UART/Wi-Fi 中直接 `up_irq_save()` 保护共享对象则明确不够。最后补读 atomic 的 CMake 接入和 P0/PM API 参考后即可汇总。

39: 
40: static_assert(CONFIG_PM_NDOMAINS >= (CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS + 1),

45:  ****************************************************************************/
